'''''Tagetes lemmonii''''', or '''Lemmon's marigold''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TALE|taxon=Tagetes lemmonii|accessdate=7 December 2015}}</ref> is a North American [[species]] of shrubby [[Tagetes|marigold]], in the family [[Asteraceae]]. Other English names for this plant include Copper Canyon daisy, mountain marigold, Mexican marigold, and Passionfruit Marigold.<ref>San Francisco Botanical Garden, {{cite web|url=https://www.sfbg.org/copy-of-cestrum-elegans-july-1|title="Featured Plant: Tagetes lemmonii"|publisher=sfbg.org|accessdate=20 February 2020|archive-date=17 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017184415/https://www.sfbg.org/copy-of-cestrum-elegans-july-1|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tagetes Passionfruit Marigold |url=https://www.paddysplants.com/product/tagetes-passionfruit-marigold/713 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=Paddys Plants Online |language=en}}</ref>

It is native to the states of [[Sonora]] and [[Sinaloa]] in northwestern Mexico as well as southern [[Arizona]] in the United States.<ref name="bonap">{{cite web|url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Tagetes%20lemmonii.png |title=Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map |publisher=bonap.net|accessdate=2015-07-05}}</ref><ref name=s>{{cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250067698 |title=Flora of North America, ''Tagetes lemmonii'' A. Gray |publisher=efloras.org|accessdate=2015-07-05}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:201211 197 San Diego Botanic Gdn - Herb Garden, Tagetes lemmonii Mountain Marigold or Mexican Marigold.jpg|thumb|left|Flowers and leaves]]
''Tagetes lemmonii'' is a shrub sometimes reaching as much as 240 cm (8 feet) tall.

Leaves are up to 12 cm (4.8 inches) long, pinnately compound into 3-5 leaflets, each leaflet narrowly lance-shaped with teeth along the edge.

===Inflorescences===
The plant produces many small [[flower heads]] in a flat-topped array, each head with 3-8 [[ray florets]] and 12-30 [[disc floret]]s. It grows in woodlands, cliffs, and moist sites.<ref name=s/>

==Taxonomy==
The species is named for [[John Gill Lemmon]], husband of American botanist [[Sarah Plummer Lemmon]].<ref name="biodiversitylibrary">{{cite book|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/8864340#page/52/mode/1up |title=Gray, Asa 1882. Proceedings of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences 19: 40–42 |year=1883 |volume=19 |publisher=biodiversitylibrary.org|accessdate=2015-07-05}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Tagetes lemmonii'' blooms from fall into spring and can sometimes be blooming for up to 10 months. It can get up to 8 feet tall by across. The foliage is pungent when disturbed.
The species is very drought tolerant in a [[Mediterranean climate]] and much used in California gardens where it tolerates light frosts without damage.
